The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Let $Q$ be any finite acyclic quiver over $k=\mathbb F_q$, with no
finite-representation-type restriction, and let $Z_-$ and $Z_+$ assign a charge in
$\mathbb H=\{z\in\mathbb C:\operatorname{Im}z>0\}$ to every vertex. Use the
subobject-first dimension completion and the Euler and skew integrations
defined on this A page. Then
$$P_{Z_-}^E=P_{Z_+}^E,\qquad P_{Z_-}^{\mathrm{sk}}=P_{Z_+}^{\mathrm{sk}}.$$
Each is a unit with constant term $1$ in its own completed quantum torus.
Consequently conjugation by the two generators defines the same continuous
automorphism on each corresponding completed torus. The products and
automorphisms are formal in the dimension completion. This is a finite-field
Hall identity only; it makes no physical state-counting identification.

derivations.claim: For a supported charge $\gamma$, put $n_\delta=\Omega_u(\gamma)\langle\delta,\gamma\rangle_{\mathrm{DSZ}}\in\mathbb Z$. Since $\ell(\gamma)>0$, the binomial expansion of $1-\varepsilon(\gamma)y^\gamma$ to any integer power is defined degreewise in the pointed completion: terms of order $k$ have degree increased by $k\ell(\gamma)$. Bilinearity gives $n_{\delta+\delta'}=n_\delta+n_{\delta'}$, so the formula for $\mathcal K_{\gamma,u}$ is multiplicative on monomials and hence on series by continuity. It fixes $y^\gamma$ because the pairing is alternating, and replacing $n_\delta$ by $-n_\delta$ gives its inverse. Finite sublevels and $\ell(\gamma)>0$ ensure each bounded-degree output uses only finitely many input terms and binomial terms. Local finiteness of the support then makes the phase-ordered composition $\mathcal S_u$ continuous and well-defined.

The formula for $\Phi$ preserves products on basis monomials: $\Phi(x^{\mathbf d}*x^{\mathbf e})=\sigma(t)^{-\langle\mathbf e,\mathbf d\rangle_Q}Y^{\rho(\mathbf d+\mathbf e)}$, while $\Phi(x^{\mathbf d})\star_\hbar\Phi(x^{\mathbf e})=\hbar^{-\langle\rho(\mathbf e),\rho(\mathbf d)\rangle_{\mathrm{DSZ}}}Y^{\rho(\mathbf d+\mathbf e)}$. The pairing identity and $\sigma(t)=\hbar$ make these expressions equal. The degree condition in the Statement makes $\Phi$ continuous on the completions.

The finite-field hypotheses of [F3] hold for the same $Q$ and the two assignments $Z_{u_-},Z_{u_+}$, since their vertex values lie in $\mathbb H$ by the common phase rotation. Therefore $P_{Z_{u_-}}^{\mathrm{sk}}=P_{Z_{u_+}}^{\mathrm{sk}}$ as units of the completed Hall skew torus.

Apply the continuous homomorphism $\Phi$ from step 1.2 to the degreewise equality in step 1.3. Equal coefficients remain equal under the coefficient embedding and charge map, so $\Phi(P_{Z_{u_-}}^{\mathrm{sk}})=\Phi(P_{Z_{u_+}}^{\mathrm{sk}})$.

Since $\Theta$ is a continuous group homomorphism on units, applying it to step 2.1 preserves equality. The Hall generator is the decreasing-phase product of the factors $J(S_{Z_u}(\phi))$; multiplicativity of $\Phi$ and $\Theta$ and the per-phase identity in [A2] therefore identify each image with the corresponding physical phase factor, in the same order. Degreewise continuity and local finiteness in [A3] pass this equality from finite truncations to the full products. [F1] supplies the second-helicity index convention, and [A1] records its choice-strength premise. Thus $\mathcal S_{u_-}=\mathcal S_{u_+}$.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Let $Q=(Q_0,Q_1,s,t)$ be a finite quiver: $Q_0$ and $Q_1$ are finite sets,
and $s,t:Q_1\to Q_0$ give the source and target of each arrow. Assume $Q$ has
no directed cycles. For a field $K$, a finite-dimensional representation $M$
assigns a finite-dimensional $K$-vector space $M_i$ to each $i\in Q_0$ and a
linear map $M_a:M_{s(a)}\to M_{t(a)}$ to each $a\in Q_1$. A morphism is a
family of linear maps at the vertices commuting with all arrow maps. Write
$\mathcal A_Q(K)$ for this category and
$\mathbf d(M)=(\dim_K M_i)_{i\in Q_0}\in\mathbb N^{Q_0}$ for its dimension
vector. For the finite-field Hall branch, fix $k=\mathbb F_q$ and write
$\mathcal A_Q=\mathcal A_Q(k)$. The next lemma proves the abelian and Euler
properties over any field; over $k$ it constructs a small finitary abelian
skeleton of $\mathcal A_Q$, so $\mathcal A_Q$ is essentially small.

For $\mathbf d,\mathbf e\in\mathbb Z^{Q_0}$ define the bilinear form
$$\chi_Q(\mathbf d,\mathbf e)=\sum_{i\in Q_0}d_i e_i-\sum_{a:i\to j}d_i e_j,$$
and its skew-symmetrization
$\langle\mathbf d,\mathbf e\rangle=\chi_Q(\mathbf d,\mathbf e)-\chi_Q(\mathbf e,\mathbf d)$.
The next lemma proves that $\chi_Q(\mathbf d(M),\mathbf d(N))$ is the
Hom-minus-Yoneda-Ext$^1$ dimension for this arrow convention.

Fix $z_i\in\mathbb H:=\{z\in\mathbb C:\operatorname{Im}z>0\}$ for each
vertex and extend $Z(\mathbf d)=\sum_i d_i z_i$ additively. If
$\mathbf d\in\mathbb N^{Q_0}$ is nonzero, then
$\operatorname{Im}Z(\mathbf d)=\sum_i d_i\operatorname{Im}z_i>0$; thus its
principal argument lies in $(0,\pi)$. For a nonzero representation $M$, put
$\phi_Z(M)=\arg Z(\mathbf d(M))/\pi\in(0,1)$. Call
$M$ **$Z$-semistable** if every nonzero subrepresentation $U\subseteq M$
satisfies $\phi_Z(U)\le\phi_Z(M)$, and **$Z$-stable** if the inequality is
strict for every proper nonzero subrepresentation.

For the semistable groupoids and stacks below, include the zero representation
as semistable without assigning it a phase. Stable objects and HN factors
remain nonzero.

For a dimension vector $\mathbf d$, let
$$\operatorname{Rep}_{\mathbf d}(Q)=\prod_{a:i\to j} \operatorname{Hom}_k(k^{d_i},k^{d_j}),\qquad G_{\mathbf d}=\prod_{i\in Q_0}\operatorname{GL}_{d_i,k}.$$
The group $G_{\mathbf d}$ acts by change of bases. Define
$\operatorname{Rep}^{ss}_{\mathbf d}(Q,Z)$ geometrically: its points over an
algebraic closure $\bar k$ are representations for which every nonzero
$\bar k$-subrepresentation satisfies the semistability inequality. The
associated quotient stack is
$\mathfrak M^{ss}_{\mathbf d}(Q,Z)=[\operatorname{Rep}^{ss}_{\mathbf d}(Q,Z)/G_{\mathbf d}]$.
For $\mathbf d=0$, set $\operatorname{Rep}^{ss}_{\mathbf0}=\operatorname{Rep}_{\mathbf0}=\operatorname{Spec}k$.
The group $G_{\mathbf0}$ is trivial, so its rational-point groupoid has one
zero object, trivial automorphism group, and cardinality $1$.
Here $[X/G]$ denotes the groupoid-valued quotient: over a scheme $S$ its
objects are $G$-torsors on $S$ with equivariant maps to $X$, and its arrows
are equivariant isomorphisms over $S$. The openness lemma below proves that
$\operatorname{Rep}^{ss}_{\mathbf d}$ is open.

For a finite groupoid $\mathcal G$, define its groupoid cardinality by
$$|\mathcal G|=\sum_{[x]\in\operatorname{Iso}(\mathcal G)} \frac{1}{|\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal G}(x)|}.$$
The rational-point groupoid of $\mathfrak M^{ss}_{\mathbf d}$ is finite, and
the finite-field descent lemma identifies it with the groupoid of finite-field
semistable representations and their isomorphisms. No Calabi–Yau structure,
potential, orientation data, vanishing cycles, or physical state-counting
identification is part of this definition.

Let $\mathbb H=\{z\in\mathbb C:\operatorname{Im}z>0\}$ and define
$\phi(z)=\arg(z)/\pi\in(0,1)$. For $z,w\in\mathbb H$, the phase of $z+w$
lies between $\phi(z)$ and $\phi(w)$, strictly between them when they are
unequal and equal to their common value when they coincide.

Let $Q$ be any finite acyclic quiver over $k=\mathbb F_q$, with no
finite-representation-type restriction, and let $Z_-$ and $Z_+$ assign a charge in
$\mathbb H=\{z\in\mathbb C:\operatorname{Im}z>0\}$ to every vertex. Use the
subobject-first dimension completion and the Euler and skew integrations
defined on this A page. Then
$$P_{Z_-}^E=P_{Z_+}^E,\qquad P_{Z_-}^{\mathrm{sk}}=P_{Z_+}^{\mathrm{sk}}.$$
Each is a unit with constant term $1$ in its own completed quantum torus.
Consequently conjugation by the two generators defines the same continuous
automorphism on each corresponding completed torus. The products and
automorphisms are formal in the dimension completion. This is a finite-field
Hall identity only; it makes no physical state-counting identification.

derivations.claim: In dimension $(1,1)$ each vertex space is $\mathbb F_q$. The two arrow maps are a pair $(r,s)\in\mathbb F_q^2$, and a change of bases $(g_m,g_d)\in(\mathbb F_q^\times)^2$ sends $(r,s)$ to $(g_m r g_d^{-1},g_m s g_d^{-1})$. Hence the zero pair is one orbit and the nonzero pairs are classified by their one-dimensional spans in $\mathbb F_q^2$, giving $|\mathbb P^1(\mathbb F_q)|=(q^2-1)/(q-1)=q+1$ nonzero isomorphism classes.

For a nonzero pair, an automorphism must satisfy $g_m r=r g_d$ and $g_m s=s g_d$; at least one arrow scalar is nonzero, so $g_m=g_d$ and the automorphism group has order $q-1$. For the zero pair every pair of base changes is allowed, so its automorphism group has order $(q-1)^2$.

The subrepresentation supported only at $m$ exists for every representation because both arrows have source $d$. The subrepresentation supported only at $d$ exists exactly for the zero pair. In the stated chamber $\phi_m<\phi_d$, [F4] places the total phase between the two vertex phases; thus every nonzero pair has only the lower-phase proper subrepresentation at $m$ and is stable, whereas the zero pair has the higher-phase subrepresentation at $d$ and is unstable. If $\phi_d<\phi_m$, the subrepresentation at $m$ has higher phase than the total for every pair, so none is semistable.

The stable groupoid cardinality in the first chamber is the sum of $q+1$ weights $1/(q-1)$, namely $(q+1)/(q-1)$. For $\mathbf d=(1,1)$ and two arrows $d\to m$, $\chi_Q(\mathbf d,\mathbf d)=1+1-2=0$, so the skew integration contributes the factor $t^0=1$ and leaves this exact coefficient.

The charge map preserves the skew form on the basis pair: the two-arrow orientation gives $\langle\mathbf e_m,\mathbf e_d\rangle_Q=2$, equal to $\langle\gamma_m,\gamma_d\rangle_{\mathrm{DSZ}}$ by [F3]. Applying [F5] to the two phase assignments proves equality of the full completed Hall generators. If the bridge in [F6] is supplied with these exact phases and pairings, the physical KS products agree by the conditional theorem. The coefficient $(q+1)/(q-1)$ remains the finite-field groupoid weight computed in step 3.1; no step identifies it with the physical index $\Omega_u(\gamma_m+\gamma_d)$.
